Abandoned Village: A abandoned village, also known as a zombie village, is a rare variant of a village that is inhabited by zombie villagers. Unlike regular villages, non-zombie villagers and iron golems don't spawn. Due to not having villagers, raids cannot occur in abandoned villages.​[more information needed]
Ancient City: An ancient city is a palatial structure found in deep dark biomes at Y level -51, harboring chests containing some items, such as disc fragments, that cannot be found anywhere else. It is also the largest structure in the game.
Bastion Remnant: Bastion remnants, also simply referred to as bastions, are large, castle-like generated structures found in the Nether in all of the biomes except basalt deltas. They generate in four distinct variants, each with a unique structure and set of loot. Piglins and piglin brutes spawn in these structures on generation, and hoglins may also spawn on generation in the bridge and hoglin stables variants. Bastion remnants are the only place to find gilded blackstone, the Pigstep music disc, the snout banner pattern and armor trim, monster spawners which spawn magma cubes, and the netherite upgrade smithing template.
Brick Pyramid: Brick pyramids were tall experimental generated structures made up exclusively of bricks present in Java Edition Infdev.
Buried Treasure: Buried treasure is a naturally generated structure that consists of a buried loot chest. The chest is buried primarily in beaches, and rarely in the ocean floor. Buried treasure is the only source of the heart of the sea, which can be used to craft a conduit. Buried treasure can be located using explorer maps.
Cold Ocean Ruins: Cold Ocean Ruins is a variant of Ocean Ruins. It's a underwater structures primarily composed of stone bricks. They are found in ocean biomes and rarely on beaches, and are inhabited by drowned and sometimes zombie nautiluses alongside them. They contain chest and suspicious gravel that contain a variety of loot, notably the buried treasure map and the sniffer egg.
Colosseum: A colosseum is a large structure found in the Potato dimension, added in 24w14potato. It houses the mega spud boss.
Desert Pyramid: A desert pyramid, commonly referred to as a desert temple, is an uncommon above ground structure found in desert biomes built mostly of sandstone. The desert pyramid contains four loot chests hidden under the floor in the center protected by a TNT trap under the floor, and a secret buried room to the side where archaeology can be performed by brushing the generated suspicious sand.
Desert Village: A desert village is a variant of Village that generate naturally in the Overworld. A plains village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems, livestock mobs and wandering traders with their trader llamas.
End City: End cities are tall structures found on the outer islands of the End. They are inhabited by shulkers and hold valuable loot, including enchanted iron and diamond tools and armor. End ships, found in some End cities, are the only source of elytra other than Creative mode and the /give command.
Farm: A farm is a generated structure in a village used for growing various crops.
Hash Well: A hash well is a feature mostly consisting of charred baked potato bricks in 24w14potato.
Igloo: An igloo is a structure sometimes generated in snowy taigas, snowy plains, or snowy slopes and built mainly of snow blocks.
Jigsaw structure:
Jigsaw structures are structures that generate using jigsaw blocks.
They are used to generate pillager outposts, villages, bastion remnants, ancient cities, trail ruins, and trial chambers.
The jigsaw structure generation can be customized using data packs in Java Edition or add-ons in Bedrock Edition.
Jungle Pyramid: A jungle pyramid or jungle temple is an above ground structure found in jungle biomes built mostly of cobblestone and mossy cobblestone. The jungle pyramid contains two loot chests, one at the end of a hallway of arrow booby traps and one hidden behind a lever puzzle.
Lunar Base: ACME Self-Building Lunar Bases were joke features that could be found on the Moon in the April Fools' snapshot 23w13a_or_b.
Mineshaft:
Mineshafts are common underground structures primarily found underground in the Overworld. They consist of interlinked 3×3 tunnels with incomplete rail lines running through them, with oak wood platforms bridging gaps or hanging in larger exposed caverns. Mineshafts are the only structures where cave spider monster spawners can be found.
A unique variant of mineshafts made out of dark oak wood can generate on the surface in badlands biomes.
Nether Fortress: A Nether fortress is an uncommon large structure made of Nether bricks found in the Nether, consisting of bridges, corridors, and towers. Nether fortresses are the only place where wither skeletons and blazes spawn. They also contain Nether wart.
Nether Fossil: Nether fossils are fossils that generate in soul sand valleys that can sometimes contain dried ghasts.
Obsidian Wall: Obsidian walls were an experimental and short-lived debugging structure made of obsidian. They were introduced in a version of Infdev released on February 27, 2010, and were removed two weeks later on March 13.
Woodland Mansion: A woodland mansion is a massive systematically-generated structure found in dark forests and pale gardens. It is often found far away from the world spawn point. A mansion is inhabited by vindicators, evokers, and allays and is one of the only places where totems of undying can be obtained. They are primarily made of dark oak wood and cobblestone, and are filled with various rooms. Besides illagers, a mansion's interior lighting is sufficiently low for other Overworld monsters to spawn.
Ocean Monument: Ocean monuments, also known as simply monuments, are rare underwater structures found in deep ocean biomes and variants. They are inhabited by guardians and elder guardians. They are the only place where sponges can be found and one of the two places where prismarine can be found; the other being ocean ruins.
Ocean Ruins: Ocean ruins are underwater structures primarily composed of stone bricks or sandstone. They are found in ocean biomes and rarely on beaches, and are inhabited by drowned and sometimes zombie nautiluses alongside them. They contain chests, suspicious sand, and suspicious gravel that contain a variety of loot, notably the buried treasure map and the sniffer egg. Ocean ruins have cold and warm underwater variants that vary from single huts to large villages.
Pillager Outpost: A pillager outpost is an assortment of generated structures inhabited by pillagers.
Plains Village: A plains village is a variant of Village that generate naturally in the Overworld. A plains village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems, livestock mobs and wandering traders with their trader llamas.
Potato Geode: A potato geode is a potato variant of an amethyst geode, added in 24w14potato.
Potato Mineshaft: A potato mineshaft is a version of the mineshaft for the Potato dimension in the 24w14potato.
Potato Village: A potato village is a joke version of the village, added in 24w14potato. It generates in the Potato dimension.
Ruined Portal: A ruined portal is a structure resembling a damaged Nether portal, which generates commonly in both the Nether and the Overworld. It contains some decoration and a loot chest around it.
Ruined Portatol: A ruined portatol is a structure added in 24w14potato. It can be located using a potato eye if the player is in the Overworld.
Savanna Village: A savanna village is a variant of Village that generate naturally in the Overworld. A plains village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems, livestock mobs and wandering traders with their trader llamas.
Shipwreck: A shipwreck is a common structure found in a oceanic biomes that resembles a sunken sailing ship.
Snowy Village: A snowy village is a variant of Village that generate naturally in the Overworld. A plains village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems, livestock mobs and wandering traders with their trader llamas.
Starting House: The starting house was a structure that acted as the starting place when first spawned in a Java Edition Indev world. It could be considered the first "structure" added to the game (though it could also be considered a feature).
Stronghold: A stronghold is a rare underground structure in the Overworld, and is the only place where an End portal can be found. Strongholds can be located by using an eye of ender.
Swamp Hut: Swamp huts (also known as witch huts) are small above ground structures that have the ability to spawn witches and black cats.
Taiga Village: A taiga village is a variant of Village that generate naturally in the Overworld. A plains village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems, livestock mobs and wandering traders with their trader llamas.
Trail Ruins: Trail ruins are buried structures that work as archaeological sites where suspicious gravel generates. They are found in heavily forested biomes and resemble ruined villages from a lost culture.
Trial Chambers:
Trial chambers are uncommon underground structures that serve as a mid-game combat challenge. They consist mostly of copper blocks and tuff bricks, and are the only place where trial spawners and vaults naturally generate. Trial chambers are also the only place where breezes spawn, whose breeze rods can be used to craft wind charges. Various materials such as heavy cores and certain armor trims are obtained exclusively by unlocking vaults in trial chambers. As it is the only source of breeze rods and heavy cores, the structure is also the location where maces are obtained.
Ominous trials can also take place here through Bad Omen, where Trial Omen causes all trial spawners to become ominous, making them more difficult and providing greater rewards.
Village:
A village is a group or complex of buildings and other above ground structures that generate naturally in the Overworld. A village is inhabited by villagers, cats, iron golems and livestock mobs. Wandering traders with their trader llamas can occasionally spawn there.
Villages are a source of resources for the player, obtained through trading, loot chests, and other materials found within the village. They are also targeted by illager raids, which are triggered when a player with the Bad Omen effect enters a village.
Warm Ocean Ruins: Warm ocean ruins are a variant of ocean ruins. It's a underwater structures primarily composed of sandstone. They are found in ocean biomes and rarely on beaches, and are inhabited by drowned and sometimes zombie nautiluses alongside them. They contain chests and suspicious sand that contain a variety of loot, notably the buried treasure map and the sniffer egg.
